_comment: US-001 shared commit-integrity oracle parity matrix. Consumed by BOTH tests/node/test-done-claim-commit-oracle.test.mjs (pure predicate + git wrapper) AND tests/test_commit_oracle.sh (zsh _commit_oracle_check against real git). Each runtime translates the abstract recipe into either injected facts (Node pure) or a real temp git repo (zsh + Node wrapper). Fields: commitStep (is there a commit exec-step exit 0), commitSha (head|unreachable|bogus|absent), advance (this-iter|first-commit|prior-only-lie|none), dirty (clean|tracked|untracked|preexisting), claimKind (build|confirmation — build claims carry a write_test step, confirmation claims carry verify_existing instead; drives isBuildClaim / the zsh jq not-build predicate; default build), commitTreeDelta (empty|nonempty|root — the claimed commit's tree vs its PARENT's: empty = git commit --allow-empty, root = no parent at all so the delta is unknowable; default nonempty), expectAsserted, expectOk, expectReason (optional — when present BOTH runtimes assert the reason string, which is how cross-leader reason parity is pinned).

scenarios.name: confirmation-claim-empty-commit-reject
scenarios._comment: G3 anti-fabrication: a confirmation/verification claim (no write_test step) whose claimed commit has the same tree as its parent. The commit landed and HEAD advanced, so every pre-G3 check passes — only the empty-tree predicate rejects it.

scenarios.name: confirmation-claim-real-commit-accept
scenarios._comment: G3 negative control: the SAME confirmation-shaped claim with a real (non-empty) commit is untouched — the new predicate must not reject confirmation claims per se, only empty ones.

scenarios.name: confirmation-claim-empty-root-commit-accept
scenarios._comment: G3 boundary: the claimed commit is the repo ROOT (no parent), so `git diff <sha>^ <sha>` has nothing to compare — the fact is `unknown` and the oracle ACCEPTS. Same shape as a shallow clone whose parent object is absent. Never an infra/GIT-FC rc-2: an expected parent-unavailable case is not a git failure.

scenarios.name: no-write-test-but-build-work-empty-commit-reject
scenarios._comment: G3 intent pin (RC-9): a refactor/doc/fix-against-existing-test iteration is BUILD work, but its claim carries no write_test step, so the classifier reads it as `confirmation` — mechanically identical facts to confirmation-claim-empty-commit-reject, and that is the point. The rejection is INTENDED here: an empty commit records no work regardless of claim type (governance §1f½, G3.a prompt wording). The classifier only bounds the new rejection's blast radius; it is not a claim that the classifier identifies verification work correctly. A claim of this shape with a NON-empty commit is covered by confirmation-claim-real-commit-accept.

scenarios.name: git-error-infra
scenarios._comment: GIT-FC (IMP-09): a git ERROR gathering the tracked-dirty set must NOT read as a clean tree. The tree here is genuinely dirty (tracked) so a false-clean read would corroborate the claim; both runtimes shim/force a git-diff failure and assert the infra result instead. gitError:true rows are handled by each harness's dedicated GIT-FC block, NOT the generic asserted/ok matrix loop (rc 2 / infra:true is outside the ok=0|1 contract).
